stories.headline: Russian drone hits Kyiv-Warsaw train 2km from Poland as 863 drones pound Ukraine

key_facts.fact: A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train about 2 kilometres from Ukraine's border with Poland on the morning of September 13; no passengers were injured.
key_facts.excerpt: Separately, a Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv–Warsaw train near Ukraine's border with Poland, Ukrzaliznytsia (Ukrainian Railways) reported. The train was about 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) from the Polish border. No passengers were injured.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 453 Shahed, Gerbera and Parodiya-type drones plus S8000 Banderol missiles overnight; 405 drones and six Banderols were intercepted, with hits at 13 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 453 Shahed and Gerbera drones, including some jet-powered Shaheds, as well as Parodiya decoy drones and S8000 Banderol missiles. Ukrainian forces intercepted 405 drones and six S8000 Banderol missiles. Hits were recorded at 13 locations.

key_facts.fact: The Ukrainian General Staff said Russia fired 863 drones at Ukraine over the previous 24 hours, one of the largest barrages of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ukrainian General Staff said Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine over the previous 24 hours, one of the largest barrages of the war.

key_facts.fact: A separate chartered train carrying former British PM Boris Johnson and security advisers to the German, UK, French and Italian governments was halted and partially evacuated on the same route around 5 a.m., returning from the Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv.
key_facts.excerpt: A separate chartered train carrying former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and senior European security officials was halted on the same route around 5 a.m. and partially evacuated as a precaution. The group, which included a top security adviser to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and security advisers from the U.K., France and Italy, was returning to Poland from the Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv.

key_facts.fact: Ukrzaliznytsia said the Ukrainian Central Monitoring Group evacuated the diplomatic train 15 minutes before the strike; ISW assessed the Kremlin conducted a precision drone strike intended to injure or kill European officials leaving Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrzaliznytsia confirmed on September 13 that European security officials had been traveling to Poland from Ukraine via the Yahodyn border crossing and that the Ukrainian Central Monitoring Group evacuated the diplomatic train 15 minutes before Russian forces struck a locomotive at the Polish border... The available reporting strongly supports the conclusion that the Kremlin conducted a precision drone strike intended to injure or kill current and former European government officials as they were leaving Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Poland's defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said drones struck 1 km and 5 km from the Polish frontier; Warsaw scrambled F-16s, helicopters and a SAAB early-warning aircraft, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Russian escalation 'is becoming a fact'.
key_facts.excerpt: "One of them struck 1 km from the border with Poland, another 5 km," he said. Warsaw scrambled F-16 fighters, helicopters and a SAAB airborne early-warning aircraft, and officials said Polish airspace was not breached.

key_facts.fact: Russian attacks killed at least six civilians and injured 43 across Ukraine over the past day, regional authorities reported on September 13.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least six civilians and injured 43 others over the past day, regional authorities reported on Sept. 13.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine struck back at Russian energy assets: a drone attack sparked a fire at an industrial facility in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, killing two and injuring 12, and Ukrainian Defence Intelligence hit the Slavyansk-ECO refinery in Krasnodar Krai.
key_facts.excerpt: two people were killed and 12 were injured following a Ukrainian drone attack which sparked a fire at an industrial facility in Nizhnekamsk, Russia's Republic of Tatarstan, home to a major oil refining and petrochemical hub... Ukraine Defence Intelligence also said it had struck the Slavyansk-ECO oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban

stories.headline: BRICS adopts New Delhi Declaration, silent on Ukraine; Xi takes 2027 chair

key_facts.fact: The 11-member BRICS grouping adopted the New Delhi Declaration on September 12 at a summit chaired by Narendra Modi, after negotiations ran into the early hours of Saturday; the text runs 45 pages and 140 points.
key_facts.excerpt: The Brics countries adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, a 45-page document containing 140 points, after intensive negotiations that continued into the early hours of Saturday.

key_facts.fact: Iran and the UAE accepted a last-minute compromise: the declaration called for 'maximum restraint' in West Asia without naming the US and Israeli strikes on Iran or Iran's subsequent strikes on Gulf neighbours.
key_facts.excerpt: India forged a consensus of BRICS countries on Saturday (September 12, 2026), after Iran and the United Arab Emirates agreed to a last-minute compromise on the language used about the war in West Asia... The statement — that did not directly mention the attacks against Iran by the United States and Israel nor Iran's subsequent strikes on its Persian Gulf neighbours, including the UAE — called for 'maximum restraint' in the war.

key_facts.fact: The declaration made no separate mention of the war in Ukraine, referring only generically to 'conflicts in many parts of the world'.
key_facts.excerpt: It made no separate mention of the Russian war in Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on September 13 that Modi and Xi actively offered their 'good offices' to help find a solution to the Ukraine conflict in bilateral meetings, and that Putin welcomed their readiness.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Putin welcomed their readiness, saying: "During their bilateral meetings, Modi and Xi took a keen interest in the Ukraine settlement and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution"

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping, attending his first visit to India in seven years, announced China will take the BRICS chairmanship in 2027 and host the 19th summit.
key_facts.excerpt: Xi Jinping announced that China will take the BRICS chairmanship in 2027 and host the 19th summit... Xi Jinping who travelled to New Delhi for the first time in seven years to attend the meeting

key_facts.fact: Modi and Putin held a bilateral of more than 45 minutes and agreed to work towards $100 billion in India-Russia bilateral trade by 2030; Putin invited Modi to Russia for the 24th annual summit.
key_facts.excerpt: India and Russia also agreed to work towards increasing bilateral trade to $100 billion by 2030 and discussed implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030. Putin invited PM Modi to Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit

key_facts.fact: Putin, who arrived with a delegation of more than 300 Russian executives, said he does not rule out European gas prices reaching $1,500 per 1,000 cubic metres.
key_facts.excerpt: He said he does not rule out European gas prices reaching $1,500 per 1,000 cubic metres as a gas crisis in Europe begins to accelerate... Putin, who arrived in New Delhi with a delegation of more than 300 Russian executives

key_facts.fact: In a rare breakthrough, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan on the sidelines at Bharat Mandapam.
key_facts.excerpt: In a rare diplomatic breakthrough, Iran's President, Mr. Pezeshkian met with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the summit at Delhi's Bharat Mandapam official venue.

stories.headline: Iranian ship struck in Strait of Hormuz as Iran-Gulf talks on a shipping lane are postponed

key_facts.fact: An Iranian cargo vessel was struck early Sunday, September 13, off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one crew member and injuring four; Iranian officials blamed a 'terrorist enemy'.
key_facts.excerpt: An Iranian cargo ship was struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one and injuring four. Officials blamed a 'terrorist enemy' as regional shipping concerns deepened.

key_facts.fact: Iran said it planned a regional foreign ministers' meeting in Oman to discuss joint management of the strait, tying any full reopening of the waterway to an end of the US blockade; commercial traffic remains sparse.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran says it plans a regional foreign ministers' meeting in Oman to discuss joint management of the strait, tying any full reopening of the waterway to an end of the U.S. blockade. Commercial traffic through the waterway remains sparse as attacks continue.

key_facts.fact: The Monday meeting between Iran and several Gulf nations to create a temporary shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz was postponed, leaving efforts to restore traffic through the chokepoint in limbo.
key_facts.excerpt: A meeting planned for Monday between Iran and several Gulf nations to create a temporary shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz was postponed, leaving efforts to increase shipments through the critical waterway in limbo.

key_facts.fact: Yemen's Houthi group said early Sunday it had struck weapons depots and command facilities at the Sharurah base in southern Saudi Arabia with a barrage of ballistic missiles and drones, warning of deeper strikes if Saudi operations continue.
key_facts.excerpt: Yemen's Houthi group said early Sunday it had carried out a coordinated strike using ballistic missiles and drones against a military installation in southern Saudi Arabia. The attack targeted weapons depots and command facilities at the Sharurah base, according to their military spokesman Yahya Saree.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense reported on Saturday that a projectile landed in the Al-Tuwal governorate of the southwestern Jazan region, injuring two people; Riyadh has not responded officially to the Houthi claim.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi authorities have not issued an official response to the Houthi claim. Earlier on Saturday, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense reported that a projectile had landed in the Al-Tuwal governorate in the southwestern Jazan region, injuring two people.

key_facts.fact: The Houthis now control western Al-Hudaydah province and have captured the coastal city of Mokha, bringing them within striking distance of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
key_facts.excerpt: The Houthis now maintain full control over the western Al-Hudaydah province and have advanced through western Taiz province, capturing the strategic coastal city of Mokha and its Red Sea port. Their territorial gains have brought the group within striking distance of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose toward $107 a barrel on Monday after rallying almost 9% last week on Middle East supply fears.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent rose toward $107 a barrel, after rallying almost 9% last week.

stories.headline: Markets price 88% odds of the Fed's first rate hike in three years as oil tops $100

key_facts.fact: Traders were pricing roughly an 87-88% chance of a 25 basis-point increase at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, which would lift the federal funds target range to 3.75%-4.00% — the first hike in three years.
key_facts.excerpt: The federal funds target range is at 3.50% to 3.75%. A quarter-point increase next Wednesday would lift it to 3.75% to 4.00%. The market moved from 67% before this week's inflation data to 87% after.

key_facts.fact: August CPI rose 0.4% from July with the annual rate at 3.4%, while core CPI rose 0.3% month on month, above the 0.2% forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: August Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% from July after increasing 0.1% in July. The annual inflation rate held at 3.4%. Both headline figures matched estimates... Core CPI increased 0.3% for the month, topping the 0.2% forecast.

key_facts.fact: Spot gold fell to about $4,331 an ounce on Monday, down roughly 0.4%, after a third consecutive weekly decline of 1.8%; silver dropped 1.0% to $63.88 and the dollar index rose 0.3% to 99.42.
key_facts.excerpt: Spot gold fell to about $4,331 an ounce, down roughly 0.4% on the day, marking a third straight weekly decline after losing 1.8% last week... The U.S. Dollar Index climbed 0.3% to 99.42, adding further pressure on gold, while silver dropped 1.0% to $63.88

key_facts.fact: US Treasury yields hit multiyear highs on Friday: the 2-year rose to 4.628%, the highest since July 2024, and the 10-year gained to 4.97% after touching 4.992%, its highest since October 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: The 2-year Treasury yield rose 7.8 basis points to 4.628%, its highest since July 2024. The 10-year gained 2.9 basis points to 4.97% after touching 4.992%, its highest since October 2023.

key_facts.fact: WTI settled at $100.05 and Brent at $104.61 on Friday; Brent still posted a weekly gain of more than 9%.
key_facts.excerpt: WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.4%. Brent finished at $104.61, down 2.8%. Brent still posted a weekly gain of more than 9%.

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump reiterated his calls for lower rates on Sunday, after weeks of public frustration with the central bank's stance.
key_facts.excerpt: the Fed could risk attract the ire of President Donald Trump, who reiterated calls for lower rates on Sunday after voicing growing frustration with the central bank's stance in recent weeks.

key_facts.fact: Gold traders are watching whether Fed Chair Kevin Warsh frames the move as a standalone adjustment or signals additional increases.
key_facts.excerpt: Gold traders are listening for whether Chair Kevin Warsh frames this as a standalone adjustment or signals additional increases.

stories.headline: J&J's Rybrevant extends survival to 34.3 months in EGFR exon 20 lung cancer

key_facts.fact: Johnson & Johnson announced on September 13 in Seoul the final overall survival analysis of the Phase 3 PAPILLON study of first-line intravenous Rybrevant (amivantamab-vmjw) plus carboplatin-pemetrexed in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations.
key_facts.excerpt: SEOUL, South Korea, Sept. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced results from the final overall survival (OS) analysis of the Phase 3 PAPILLON study evaluating first-line intravenous (IV) RYBREVANT (amivantamab-vmjw) plus carboplatin-pemetrexed chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone

key_facts.fact: Patients on the combination reached a median overall survival of 34.3 months versus 27.9 months on chemotherapy alone — the longest reported median OS in this population, nearly twice the historical median.
key_facts.excerpt: Patients treated with the combination achieved a median OS of nearly three years (34.3 months), compared with 27.9 months for chemotherapy alone... This represents the longest reported median OS in this patient population, which is nearly twice the historical median.

key_facts.fact: The headline comparison did not reach statistical significance (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.66-1.14; P=0.307) because 76% of eligible chemotherapy-arm patients crossed over to Rybrevant after progression.
key_facts.excerpt: In the protocol-specified final analysis, RYBREVANT plus chemotherapy demonstrated a median OS of nearly three years (34.3 months) compared to approximately two years (27.9 months) for chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio [HR], 0.87; 95 percent confidence interval [CI], 0.66-1.14; P=0.307).

key_facts.fact: A prespecified crossover-adjusted analysis showed a 43% reduction in the risk of death (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.39-0.82; nominal P=0.003).
key_facts.excerpt: A prespecified analysis accounting for crossover to RYBREVANT in the chemotherapy arm showed a significant overall survival benefit with RYBREVANT plus chemotherapy, reducing the risk of death by 43 percent (HR, 0.57; 95 percent CI, 0.39-0.82; nominal P=0.003).

key_facts.fact: The combination extended progression-free survival through second progression by more than 10 months (28.3 vs 17.5 months; HR 0.59; nominal P<0.0001), with 12% of patients still on first-line treatment at cutoff versus none in the chemotherapy arm.
key_facts.excerpt: extending progression-free survival through second disease progression (PFS2) by more than 10 months compared with chemotherapy alone (28.3 vs. 17.5 months; HR, 0.59; 95 percent CI, 0.45-0.77; nominal P<0.0001). Twelve percent of patients remained on first-line treatment at the clinical cutoff compared with no patients in the chemotherapy arm.

key_facts.fact: PAPILLON (NCT04538664) enrolled 308 patients in a randomized, open-label Phase 3 design with progression-free survival as the primary endpoint.
key_facts.excerpt: PAPILLON (NCT04538664), which enrolled 308 patients, is a randomized, open-label Phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of RYBREVANT in combination with chemotherapy, compared with chemotherapy alone

stories.headline: SpaceX flies 700th Falcon mission, completing SES's O3b mPOWER constellation

key_facts.fact: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 2:49 p.m. EDT on September 13 carrying the final three satellites for SES's O3b mPOWER constellation.
key_facts.excerpt: A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station today at 2:49 p.m. EDT (1849 GMT), carrying the final three satellites for Luxembourg-based SES' O3b mPOWER constellation.

key_facts.fact: It was the 700th mission to date for SpaceX's Falcon rocket family, which began with the Falcon 1 debut in March 2006.
key_facts.excerpt: It was the 700th mission to date for SpaceX's Falcon rocket family, according to the company. That family first spread its wings in March 2006 when the Falcon 1 debuted.

key_facts.fact: The flight was SpaceX's 107th orbital mission of the year and the 105th Falcon 9 launch of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's launch was SpaceX's 107th orbital mission of the year. The Falcon 9 has performed 105 of those flights, with the Falcon Heavy conducting the other two.

key_facts.fact: The satellites were deployed at 5,000 miles (8,000 km) in medium Earth orbit over a 14-minute span starting roughly 33.5 minutes after launch, completing a constellation that already had 10 O3b mPOWER satellites in orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellites were deployed as scheduled, being released at an altitude of 5,000 miles (8,000 kilometers) over a 14-minute span starting roughly 33.5 minutes after launch. SES already operates 10 O3b mPOWER satellites in MEO.

key_facts.fact: It was the 29th flight for booster B1080, which previously flew Ax-2, Euclid, Ax-3, CRS-30 and 22 Starlink missions, and landed on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas.
key_facts.excerpt: This will be the 29th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously supported Ax-2, Euclid, Ax-3, CRS-30, SES ASTRA 1P, NG-21, and 22 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage will land on the A Shortfall of Gravitas droneship

key_facts.fact: It was SpaceX's fifth launch for the O3b constellation and its 20th launch for SES overall; the two fairing halves flew for the 27th and 10th times.
key_facts.excerpt: This was SpaceX's fifth launch for this SES constellation. It has now placed thirteen of these type satellites into orbit, and has completed 20 launches for SES overall... The two fairings completed their 27th and 10th flights respectively.

stories.headline: India's Solar Industries bids $1.4 billion for South Africa's Omnia Holdings

key_facts.fact: Solar Industries India agreed to acquire South African industrial-explosives and fertilizer group Omnia Holdings for 21.8 billion rand ($1.4 billion), seeking to expand in African mining and agriculture.
key_facts.excerpt: Solar Industries India Ltd. agreed to acquire South African industrial-explosives and fertilizer firm Omnia Holdings Ltd. for 21.8 billion rand ($1.4 billion), seeking to expand in the continent's mining and agriculture industries.

key_facts.fact: Omnia said on Monday, September 14, that it had received the all-cash firm intention offer from Solar SA Investments, a wholly owned subsidiary of Solar Overseas Mauritius, itself a unit of Solar Industries India.
key_facts.excerpt: Fertiliser and explosives group Omnia has received a R21.8bn all-cash buyout offer from Indian company Solar Group, the company said on Monday. Omnia said on Monday that Solar SA Investments, a wholly owned subsidiary of Solar Overseas Mauritius, which is a unit of Solar Industries India, has made a firm intention offer for Omnia.

key_facts.fact: If the deal proceeds, Omnia will be delisted from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and A2X.
key_facts.excerpt: Proposed deal, if successful, to result in Omnia delisting from JSE and A2X

key_facts.fact: Omnia's board said that after extensive due diligence and negotiations it intends to recommend the scheme to shareholders, and that the offer has broad shareholder support plus an irrevocable unconditional bank guarantee for the cash consideration.
key_facts.excerpt: Omnia said that following extensive due diligence and negotiations, its board intends to recommend the scheme to shareholders. "The proposed transaction has secured broad shareholder support and is backed by an irrevocable unconditional bank guarantee for the cash consideration," it said.
